quiz.title: CBSE Class 12 Maths 2012 Practice Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight board-level questions in the style of the 2012 paper, spanning calculus, matrices, vectors, three-dimensional geometry, probability, integrals and differential equations. Choose an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: If y = e<sup>2x</sup>, then d<sup>2</sup>y/dx<sup>2</sup> equals:
questions.explanation: Differentiating twice: dy/dx = 2e<sup>2x</sup>, and d<sup>2</sup>y/dx<sup>2</sup> = 4e<sup>2x</sup>. Each derivative brings down a factor of 2.

questions.q: If A is a 3 × 3 matrix with det(A) = 2, then det(2A) equals:
questions.explanation: For an n × n matrix, det(kA) = k<sup>n</sup>det(A). Here det(2A) = 2<sup>3</sup> × 2 = 8 × 2 = 16.

questions.q: If a and b are vectors with a · b = 6, |a| = 3 and |b| = 4, the angle between them is:
The direction cosines of the x-axis are:
questions.explanation: The x-axis points along the unit vector i, so its direction cosines are (1, 0, 0).

questions.q: Two fair coins are tossed together. The probability of getting exactly one head is:
questions.explanation: The outcomes are HH, HT, TH, TT. Exactly one head occurs in HT and TH, so the probability is 2/4 = 1/2.

questions.q: Evaluate ∫ from 0 to π/2 of cos x dx.
questions.explanation: The antiderivative of cos x is sin x, so the value is sin(π/2) − sin(0) = 1 − 0 = 1.

questions.q: The order of the differential equation (d<sup>2</sup>y/dx<sup>2</sup>)<sup>2</sup> + (dy/dx)<sup>3</sup> + y = 0 is:
questions.explanation: The order is the highest derivative present. Here the highest is d<sup>2</sup>y/dx<sup>2</sup>, so the order is 2 (the powers do not affect order).

questions.q: The function f(x) = x<sup>2</sup> is strictly increasing on the interval:
questions.explanation: f′(x) = 2x, which is positive only when x > 0. So f is strictly increasing on (0, ∞).

faq.q: How difficult was the CBSE Class 12 Mathematics 2012 paper?
faq.a: The 2012 paper stuck to the familiar board pattern of that period, mixing one-mark, four-mark and six-mark questions across calculus, algebra, vectors and probability. Nearly every question mapped straight onto an NCERT concept, so a student who had finished the textbook found it manageable.

faq.q: Which topics carried the most marks in the 2012 paper?
faq.a: Calculus led the way, as it almost always does in Class 12 — differentiation, applications of derivatives, integrals and differential equations together made up the biggest block. Matrices, determinants, vectors, three-dimensional geometry, probability and linear programming shared the remaining marks.

faq.q: Is the 2012 paper still useful for today's students?
faq.a: Yes. Core chapters like integrals, vectors and differential equations have changed little, so the paper is solid practice for accuracy and timing. Do cross-check the current CBSE blueprint for the exact weightage and any topics that have since been trimmed.

faq.q: What is the best way to practise with an old board paper?
faq.a: Attempt it in one timed sitting with no notes, then grade it honestly against the answer key. List every mistake, go back to that concept in your textbook, and re-solve similar questions a few days later so the fix truly sticks.
